# Project Summary

# Set-Up Chunks

## Loading packages

```{r}
# Standard data manipulation/visualization and data loading packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)

# Mixed effect model packages
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)

# Akaike Information Criterion
library(cAIC4)

# Estimated marginal means for post-hoc testing
library(emmeans)
```

## Loading data sets

```{r}
# Saving Excel data to variables with read_excel
Height_Data_Raw = read_excel(
  "Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
  sheet = "Seedling Heights"
  )

Moist_Data_Raw = read_excel(
  "Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
  sheet = "Soil Moisture"
  )

SPAD_Data_Raw = read_excel(
  "Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
   sheet = "SPAD", na = "NA")
```

# 1. Cleaning Data with dplyr

## 1.1. Cleaning SPAD Data

```{r}
# Visual check to see if data looks as expected
SPAD_Data_Raw

# Cleaning SPAD data
SPAD_Data_Clean = SPAD_Data_Raw |>
  
  # Filtering out NA rows (there's a billion for some reason) with filter()
  filter(is.na(Treatment) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Creating new column for sapling number with separate()
  separate(Tag_Num,
    c("Tag_Num", "Sapling_Num"), 
    3, extra = "merge", fill = "right"
  ) |>
  
  # Converting Sapling_Num into characters and adding NA values where applicable
  # with mutate() and case_when()
  mutate(Sapling_Num = case_when(
    Sapling_Num == "A1" ~ "A",
    Sapling_Num == "A2" ~ "B",
    Sapling_Num == "A3" ~ "C",
    Sapling_Num == "" ~ NA,
    is.character(Sapling_Num) == TRUE ~ Sapling_Num
    )
  ) |>
  
  # Converting Sapling_Num to factor with mutate()
  mutate(Sapling_Num = as.factor(Sapling_Num)) |>
  
  # Adding indicator for multiple saplings for future use with mutate()
  mutate(Multiple_Seedling = case_when(
    is.na(Sapling_Num) == FALSE ~ TRUE,
    is.na(Sapling_Num) == TRUE ~ FALSE
    ),
    .after = Sapling_Num
  ) |>
  
  # Turning Multiple_Seedling into a factor with mutate()
  mutate(Multiple_Seedling = as.factor(Multiple_Seedling))
  
# Visual verification
SPAD_Data_Clean

# Removing QAQC columns to the right of Notes by identifying its column number with which() and then selecting only the columns to the left
Notes_colnum_SPAD = which(colnames(SPAD_Data_Clean) == "Notes")
SPAD_Data_Clean = SPAD_Data_Clean[1:Notes_colnum_SPAD]

# Visual verification
SPAD_Data_Clean

# Creating column of unique identifier numbers with mutate()
SPAD_Data_Clean = SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(ID_num = row_number(), .before = Notes)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Data_Clean

# Converting Leaf columns into Leaf_Num column with pivot_longer()
SPAD_Data_Clean = SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Leaf_Num", values_to = "SPAD_Value", cols = 10:15) |>
  
  # Removing "Leaf" from Leaf_Num with separate()
  separate(Leaf_Num,
    c("Leaf", "Leaf_Num"), 
    4, extra = "merge", fill = "left"
  ) |>
  
  # Removing Leaf with select()
  select(-Leaf)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Data_Clean

# Blanket fix for each data type that's wrong with mutate()
SPAD_Data_Clean = SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(Tag_Num = as.integer(Tag_Num)) |>
  mutate(Num_leaves = as.integer(Num_leaves)) |>
  mutate(Leaf_Num = as.integer(Leaf_Num)) |>
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date))

# Visual verification
SPAD_Data_Clean
```

## 1.2. Cleaning Soil Moisture Data

```{r}
# Visual check to see if data looks as expected
Moist_Data_Raw

# Cleaning soil moisture data
Moist_Data_Clean = Moist_Data_Raw |> 
  
  # Removing excess NA rows with filter()
  filter(is.na(Treatment) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Changing "NA" to actual native NA value with mutate() and case_when()
  mutate(VWC1_perc = case_when(
    VWC1_perc == "NA" ~ NA,
    VWC1_perc != "NA" ~ VWC1_perc
  )
  ) |>
  mutate(PER1_ms = case_when(
    PER1_ms == "NA" ~ NA,
    PER1_ms != "NA" ~ PER1_ms
  )
  ) |>
  mutate(VWC2_perc = case_when(
    VWC2_perc == "NA" ~ NA,
    VWC2_perc != "NA" ~ VWC2_perc
  )
  ) |>
  mutate(PER2_ms = case_when(
    PER2_ms == "NA" ~ NA,
    PER2_ms != "NA" ~ PER2_ms
  )
  ) |>
  mutate(VWC3_perc = case_when(
    VWC3_perc == "NA" ~ NA,
    VWC3_perc != "NA" ~ VWC3_perc
  )
  ) |>
  mutate(PER3_ms = case_when(
    PER3_ms == "NA" ~ NA,
    PER3_ms != "NA" ~ PER3_ms
  )
  )

# Visual verification
Moist_Data_Clean

# Removing QAQC columns to the right of Notes by identifying its column number with which() and then selecting only the columns to the left
Notes_colnum_Moist = which(colnames(Moist_Data_Clean) == "Notes")
Moist_Data_Clean = Moist_Data_Clean[1:Notes_colnum_Moist]

# Visual verification
Moist_Data_Clean

# Creating column of unique identifier numbers with mutate()
Moist_Data_Clean = Moist_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(ID_num = row_number())

# Visual verification
Moist_Data_Clean

# Converting VWC/PER columns into VWC_or_PER and value columns with pivot_longer()
Moist_Data_Clean = Moist_Data_Clean |>
  pivot_longer(names_to = "VWC_or_PER", values_to = "value", cols = 6:11) |>
  
  # Removing tail end of name from VWC_or_PER with separate()
  separate(VWC_or_PER,
           c("VWC_or_PER", "type"), 
           "_"
  ) |>
  
  # Separating VWC_or_PER again with separate() to create a new measure_num column
  separate(VWC_or_PER,
           c("VWC_or_PER", "measure_num"),
           3, extra = "merge", fill = "right"
  ) |>
  
  # Removing type and ID_num columns with select()
  select(-type, -ID_num) |>
  
  # Removing NA values with filter()
  filter(is.na(value) == FALSE)

# Visual verification
Moist_Data_Clean

# Blanket fixing data types with mutate()
Moist_Data_Clean = Moist_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(measure_num = as.integer(measure_num)) |>
  mutate(value = as.double(value)) |>
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date))

# Visual verification
Moist_Data_Clean
```

## 1.3. Cleaning Height Data

```{r}
# Visual check to see if data looks as expected
Height_Data_Raw
  
# Cleaning Height_Data
Height_Data_Clean = Height_Data_Raw |>
  
  # Remove NA rows
  filter(is.na(Treatment) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Changing alphanumeric Sapling_AB_etc values to characters
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = case_when(
    Sapling_AB_etc == "A1" ~ "A",
    Sapling_AB_etc == "A2" ~ "B",
    Sapling_AB_etc == "A3" ~ "C",
    is.na(Sapling_AB_etc) == TRUE ~ NA
    )
  ) |>
  
  # Adding indicator for multiple saplings for future use with mutate()
  mutate(Multiple_Seedling = case_when(
    is.na(Sapling_AB_etc) == FALSE ~ TRUE,
    is.na(Sapling_AB_etc) == TRUE ~ FALSE
  ),
  .after = Sapling_AB_etc
  ) |>
  
  # Turning Multiple_Seedling into a factor with mutate()
  mutate(Multiple_Seedling = as.factor(Multiple_Seedling)) |>
  
  # Removing that one random NA value in Dead_Alive
  filter(is.na(Dead_Alive) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Removing any treatment IDs that are incorrect
  filter(Treatment %in% c("AC", "DT", "NR", "OS"))

# Visual verification
Height_Data_Clean

# Removing QAQC data
Notes_colnum_Height = which(colnames(Height_Data_Clean) == "Notes")
Height_Data_Clean = Height_Data_Clean[1:Notes_colnum_Height]

# Visual verification
Height_Data_Clean

# Blanket fixing data types with mutate()
Height_Data_Clean = Height_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(Tag_Num = as.integer(Tag_Num)) |>
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date))

# Visual verification
Height_Data_Clean

# Editing in missing Sapling_AB_etc data with mutate() and replace(). I'm doing this manually because trying to select for randomly distributed values in a column sucks.
Height_Data_Clean = Height_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 1, "A")) |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 2, "B")) |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 10, "B")) |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 11, "A")) |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 29, "A")) |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 30, "B")) |>
  mutate(Sapling_AB_etc = replace(Sapling_AB_etc, 31, "C")) |>
  
  # Repeating call creating indicator for multiple saplings with mutate()
  mutate(Multiple_Seedling = case_when(
    is.na(Sapling_AB_etc) == FALSE ~ TRUE,
    is.na(Sapling_AB_etc) == TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

# Visual verification
Height_Data_Clean
```

# 2. Statistical Analysis

We want to establish that the storm that occurred did not modify any relationships in our measurements. As such, we will conduct regressions for SPAD value, seedling height, and leaf count with volumetric water content as the predictor for before and after the storm.

## 2.1. Evaluating VWC by Day

## 2.1. Regression Testing with SPAD_Value \~ VWC

#### Combining SPAD and Soil Moisture Data

```{r}
# Cleaning up soil moisture data more to prep it for combination
Moist_condensed = Moist_Data_Clean |>
  
  # Removing PER measurements with filter()
  filter(VWC_or_PER == "VWC") |>
  
  # Condensing VWC measurements to an average of the three measurements with
  # summarise()
  group_by(Treatment, Block) |>
  mutate(
    VWC = mean(as.double(value), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  
  # Removing excess columns with select()
  select(-VWC_or_PER, -measure_num, -value, -Team, -Entered_By) |>
  
  # Removing duplicate rows with distinct()
  distinct(VWC, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  
  # Removing Block 4 Natural Recruits due to them having no data
  filter(is.na(VWC) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Creating join-friendly date column by editing dates with mutate()
  mutate(Day = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "1",
    Date != "2026-10-08" ~ "2"
  ),
  .before = Block
  ) |>
  
  # Swapping new date column to a Factor with mutate()
  mutate(Day = as.factor(Day)) |>
  
  # Removing Date column with select()
  select(-Date)

# Visual verification
Moist_condensed

# Cleaning up SPAD data more to prep it for combination
SPAD_condensed = SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  
  # Removing Leaf_Num with select() so it doesn't complicate our math
  select(-Leaf_Num) |>
  
  # Removing excess metadata columns with select()
  select(-Team, -Entered_By) |>
  
  # Taking mean SPAD value per plant with mutate()
  group_by(ID_num, Sapling_Num) |>
  mutate(SPAD_Value = mean(SPAD_Value, na.rm = TRUE, .before = ID_num)) |>
  
  # Removing duplicate rows with distinct()
  distinct(SPAD_Value, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  
  # Creating join-friendly date column by editing dates with mutate()
  mutate(Day = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "1",
    Date != "2026-10-08" ~ "2"
  ),
  .before = Block
  ) |>
  
  # Swapping new date column to a Factor with mutate()
  mutate(Day = as.factor(Day)) |>
  
  # Removing Date column with select()
  select(-Date)

# Visual verification
SPAD_condensed

# Combining tibbles with left_join() to blend identical columns
SPAD_Moist_combined = left_join(SPAD_condensed, Moist_condensed,
                                join_by(Block, Treatment, Day)
)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Moist_combined

# Removing NA values with filter()
SPAD_Moist_combined = SPAD_Moist_combined |>
  filter(is.na(VWC) == FALSE) |>
  filter(is.na(SPAD_Value) == FALSE)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Moist_combined
```

#### Initial Visualization of SPAD_Value \~ VWC

Since there was a rainstorm between the two sampling days, we'll be faceting all graphs by Day to ensure this doesn't impact our visualizations.

```{r}
# Generating scatter plot with a best-fit line using ggplot() + geom_point() + geom_smooth()
SPAD_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = SPAD_Value) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "SPAD value"
  )
```

There are several outlier data points at the top and bottom of the graph. We will investigate our data to see why this is occurring.

```{r}
# Visualizing data to identify outliers
SPAD_Moist_combined

# Removing outliers with filter()
SPAD_Moist_combined = SPAD_Moist_combined |>
  filter(Num_leaves != 0)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Moist_combined
```

The lower outlier points were SPAD values taken from dead plants. With those removed, we will re-visualize our data.

```{r}
SPAD_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = SPAD_Value) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scale = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "SPAD value"
  )
```

Scatter plot of SPAD value as a function of volumetric water content, faceted by sampling day. While volumetric water content does increase between the two days due to the storm the relationship with SPAD value appears approximately the same, exhibiting an extremely weak positive relationship. This likely indicates that volumetric water content alone is not the primary determinant of SPAD value.

#### Checking Prerequisites for a Linear Regression

```{r}
# Splitting the combined data into two separate tibbles by Day using filter()
SPAD_Moist_Day1 = SPAD_Moist_combined |>
  filter(Day == 1)

SPAD_Moist_Day2 = SPAD_Moist_combined |>
  filter(Day == 2)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Moist_Day1
SPAD_Moist_Day2

# Creating mixed effect models for each Day using lmer() with Treatment, Multiple_Seedling, and Block as random effects
SPAD_Moist_Day1_Model = lmer(
  SPAD_Value ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = SPAD_Moist_Day1)

SPAD_Moist_Day2_Model = lmer(
  SPAD_Value ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = SPAD_Moist_Day2)

# Checking residuals vs. fitted plot for our models with plot()
plot(SPAD_Moist_Day1_Model)
plot(SPAD_Moist_Day2_Model)

# Checking normality of SPAD_Value with hist()
hist(x = SPAD_Moist_Day1$SPAD_Value)
hist(x = SPAD_Moist_Day2$SPAD_Value)
```

Our Day 1 data have sufficient homogeneity of distribution and appear to normal. Day 2 does have homogeneity of variance but is skewed slightly, however we will still assume normality since our sample size is small. We can thus continue with a simple regression test.

#### Conducting Regression Test

```{r}
# Reviewing summary of linear models with summary()
summary(SPAD_Moist_Day1_Model)
summary(SPAD_Moist_Day2_Model)
```

A model of SPAD value as a function of VWC with block integrated as a random effect and no interactions with treatment showed no significant relationship between the two measurements on either day (p1 = 0.32, p2 = 0.96). We thus cannot reject our null hypothesis and lack support for a relationship between the two values. At the very least, VWC alone is not the primary driver of plant health seemingly. We will conduct an identical regression for plant height to explore this further.

#### Visualizing Regression Results

```{r}
# Generating scatter plot with no best-fit line using ggplot() + geom_point() + geom_smooth()
SPAD_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = SPAD_Value) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  geom_text(label = c("p = 0.32"),
            x = 0.25, y = 45) +
  geom_text(label = c("p = 0.96"),
            x = 7, y = 45) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "SPAD value"
  )
```

Scatter plot of SPAD value as a function of volumetric water content across all treatment types, faceted by day. Results of a simple regression are displayed on each facet at the top left of each facet. There appears to be no relationship between SPAD value and volumetric water content both before and after the rainstorm occurred. This could be the result of SPAD value being determined by a combination of multiple factors, not just volumetric water content alone, but could equally be a function of soil water content being insufficient to support oak sapling development. Plant health could also be overall poor and yellowing the seedling's leaves.

## 2.2. Regression Testing with Plant Height \~ VWC

#### Combining Height and VWC data

```{r}
# Cleaning Height data for combination, again selecting for live plants only with filter()
Height_condensed = Height_Data_Clean |>
  
  # Removing excess metadata columns with select()
  select(-Team, -Data_Entered_By) |>
  
  # Taking mean of plant heights at each tag with mutate()
  group_by(Tag_Num, Sapling_AB_etc) |>
  mutate(Seedling_Ht_cm = mean(Seedling_Ht_cm)) |>
  
  # Creating join-friendly date column by editing dates with mutate()
  mutate(Day = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "1",
    Date != "2026-10-08" ~ "2"
  )
  ) |>
  
  # Swapping new date column to a Factor with mutate()
  mutate(Day = as.factor(Day)) |>
  
  # Removing Date column with select()
  select(-Date)

# Visual verification
Height_condensed

# Combining tibbles with left_join() to blend identical columns
Height_Moist_combined = left_join(Height_condensed, Moist_condensed,
                                  join_by(Block, Treatment, Day)
)

# Visual verification
Height_Moist_combined

# Removing NA values of VWC with filter()
Height_Moist_combined = Height_Moist_combined |>
  filter(is.na(VWC) == FALSE)

# Visual verification
Height_Moist_combined
```

#### Initial Visualization of Height \~ VWC

We'll again be faceting by Day for all these graphs.

```{r}
# Generating scatter plot with a best fit line using ggplot() + geom_point() + geom_smooth()
Height_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric Water Content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Plant Height (in cm)"
  )
```

We can see several outliers skewing our data and will need to investigate them before we can continue. Dead plant data also seems to be doing nothing but add noise to the graph, so we'll remove those too.

```{r}
# Removing dead plants from our data
Height_Moist_Alive = Height_Moist_combined |>
  filter(Seedling_Ht_cm > 0)

# Visualizing data to verify integrity and check outliers
Height_Moist_Alive
```

There's no reason to drop any of these outliers so we'll just move forward for now.

```{r}
Height_Moist_Alive |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric Water Content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Plant Height (in cm)"
  )
```

Scatter plot of plant height as a function of volumetric water content, faceted by day with a line-of-best-fit graphed over the data. The relationship between plant height does appear to differ between sampling days, which could be the result of the rainstorm that occurred, but Day 1 has several large plants that could be skewing the relationship between these measurements. At a glance we might at least assume that there is a weakly negative relationship pre-storm and a weakly positive relationship post-storm.

#### Checking Prerequisites for A Linear Regression

```{r}
# Splitting our data by Day using filter()
Height_Moist_Day1 = Height_Moist_Alive |>
  filter(Day == 1)

Height_Moist_Day2 = Height_Moist_Alive |>
  filter(Day == 2)

# Visual verification
Height_Moist_Day1
Height_Moist_Day2

# Creating mixed effect models for each Day with lmer(), with Treatment, Multiple_Seedling, and Block as random effects
Height_Moist_Day1_Model = lmer(
  Seedling_Ht_cm ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = Height_Moist_Day1)

Height_Moist_Day2_Model = lmer(
  Seedling_Ht_cm ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = Height_Moist_Day2)

# Checking plot of residuals vs. fitted for both models with plot()
plot(Height_Moist_Day1_Model)
plot(Height_Moist_Day2_Model)
```

Day 1's model, unsurprisingly, has no homogeneity of variance. We will try a log transformation on the data for this model.

```{r}
# Creating mixed effect model for Day 1 with lmer(), with Treatment, Multiple_Seedling, and Block as random effects and a log() transformation
Height_Moist_Day1_Model = lmer(
  log(Seedling_Ht_cm) ~ log(VWC) + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) +
    (1|Block), data = Height_Moist_Day1)

# Checking plot of residuals vs. fitted for this model
plot(Height_Moist_Day1_Model)
```

This has established homogeneity of variance, so we will continue with this model and check for normality.

```{r}
# Checking normality of both models with hist()
hist(x = Height_Moist_Day1$Seedling_Ht_cm)
hist(x = Height_Moist_Day2$Seedling_Ht_cm)
```

Day 2's data is roughly normal but Day 1 is noticeably skewed. Since our sample size for that day is small, however, we will assume normality and continue with a simple regression test.

#### Conducting Simple Regression Test

```{r}
# Reading summary table of our models with summary()
summary(Height_Moist_Day1_Model)
summary(Height_Moist_Day2_Model)
```

A model of plant height as a function of volumetric water content, with block, treatment, and multiple saplings integrated as random effects, showed no significant relationship between the two measurements on either day (p1 = 0.189, p2 = 0.396). We thus cannot reject our null hypothesis and lack support for a relationship between the two values. Much like in the case of leaf count, volumetric water content does not appear to be the sole predictor of plant height.

#### Visualizing Regression Results

```{r}
# Creating scatter plot for Day 1 with ggplot() + geom_point(), log() transformed in aes()
Height_Moist_Day1 |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = log(VWC), y = log(Seedling_Ht_cm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(
    label = c("p = 0.189"),
    x = -3.25, y = 4
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Log volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Log seedling height (in cm)"
  )

# Creating scatter plot for Day 1 with ggplot() + geom_point()
Height_Moist_Day2 |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = Seedling_Ht_cm) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(
    label = c("p = 0.396"),
    x = 6.5, y = 20
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Seedling height (in cm)"
  )
```

*Figure 1.* Scatter plot of log seedling height as a function of log volumetric water content for data collected on sampling day 1. Results of a simple linear regression are noted in the top left of the graph. There appears to be no relationship between volumetric water content and seedling height before the rainstorm.

*Figure 2.* Scatter plot of seedling height as a function of volumetric water content for data collected on sampling day 2. Results of a simple linear regression are noted in the top left of the graph. There appears to be no relationship between volumetric water content and seedling height after the rainstorm.

These results could suggest that seedling health is determined by multiple different factors, as was proposed in the discussion of regression tests on volumetric water content and leaf count, but again could just be the result of stochastic effects in the environment.

## 2.3. Regression Testing with Leaf Count \~ VWC

#### Combining Leaf Count and Soil Moisture Data

We can reuse our cleaned data from the SPAD value \~ VWC regression, as that retained data on leaf count.

```{r}
# Visual verification
SPAD_condensed

# Cleaning data further to fit leaf count testing better
Leaf_condensed = SPAD_condensed |>
  
  # Preemptively removing NA SPAD values and leaf counts of 0 using filter() to fit
  # with previous cleaning done to SPAD data
  filter(is.na(SPAD_Value) == FALSE) |>
  filter(Num_leaves > 0) |>
  
  # Removing duplicated leaf count values with distinct()
  group_by(ID_num, Sapling_Num) |>
  distinct(Num_leaves, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Visual verification
Leaf_condensed

# Combining tibbles with left_join() to blend identical columns
Leaf_Moist_combined = left_join(Leaf_condensed, Moist_condensed,
                                join_by(Block, Treatment, Day)
)

# Visual verification
Leaf_Moist_combined

# Removing NA values of VWC with filter()
Leaf_Moist_combined = Leaf_Moist_combined |>
  filter(is.na(VWC) == FALSE)

# Visual verification
Leaf_Moist_combined
```

#### Initial Visualization of Leaf Count \~ VWC

```{r}
# Creating scatter plot with a best-fit-line using ggplot() + geom_point() + geom_smooth(), faceted using facet_wrap()
Leaf_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = Num_leaves) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Leaf count"
  )
```

This is clearly skewed by several outlier data points. We will visually check our data to investigate why.

```{r}
# Visual check for outliers
Leaf_Moist_combined
```

Since there is no reason to remove these outliers, we'll test a log transformation.

```{r}
# Creating scatter plot with a best-fit-line using ggplot() + geom_point() + geom_smooth(), faceted using facet_wrap() and with a log() transformation applied to aes()
Leaf_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = log(VWC), y = log(Num_leaves)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Leaf count"
  )
```

This has unfortunately fixed nothing. We'll have to account for unequal variance in our model.

```{r}
# Creating scatter plot with a best-fit-line using ggplot() + geom_point() + geom_smooth(), faceted using facet_wrap()
Leaf_Moist_combined |> ggplot() +
  aes(x = VWC, y = Num_leaves) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Day)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~Day, scales = "free_x") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Volumetric water content (as a percentage)",
    y = "Leaf count"
  )
```

Scatter plot of leaf count as a function of volumetric water count, faceted by sampling day. Visuals are heavily skewed by a few outlier data points. Attempting to ignore the skew, there appears to be no noticeable relationship between leaf count and volumetric water content both before and after the storm.

#### Checking Prerequisites for a Linear Regression

```{r}
# Splitting the combined data into two separate tibbles by Day using filter()
Leaf_Moist_Day1 = Leaf_Moist_combined |>
  filter(Day == 1)

Leaf_Moist_Day2 = Leaf_Moist_combined |>
  filter(Day == 2)

# Visual verification
Leaf_Moist_Day1
Leaf_Moist_Day2

# Creating mixed effect models for each Day using lmer() with Treatment, Multiple_Seedling, and Block as random effects
Leaf_Moist_Day1_Model = lmer(
  Num_leaves ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = SPAD_Moist_Day1)

Leaf_Moist_Day2_Model = lmer(
  Num_leaves ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = Leaf_Moist_Day2)

# Viewing plot of residuals vs. fitted for our models with plot()
plot(Leaf_Moist_Day1_Model)
plot(Leaf_Moist_Day2_Model)
```

Unsurprisingly, our residuals show unequal variance. We will need to weigh our models for variance to account for this.

# Same weighting issue as others

```{r}
Leaf_Day1_variance = varPower(Leaf_Moist_Day1$Num_leaves,
  ~Leaf_Moist_Day2$VWC)
Leaf_Day2_variance = varPower(Leaf_Moist_Day2$Num_leaves,
  ~Leaf_Moist_Day2$VWC)

Leaf_Moist_Day1_Model = lmer(
  Num_leaves ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = SPAD_Moist_Day1, weights = varWeights(Leaf_Day1_variance))

Leaf_Moist_Day2_Model = lmer(
  Num_leaves ~ VWC + (1|Treatment) + (1|Multiple_Seedling) + (1|Block),
  data = Leaf_Moist_Day2, weights = varWeights(Leaf_Day2_variance))

hist(Leaf_Moist_Day1$Num_leaves)
hist(Leaf_Moist_Day2$Num_leaves)
```

Our models are still heavily skewed but we'll assume normality due to low sample size. Thus, we'll continue with a simple mixed-effects regression test.

#### Conducting Simple Regression Test

```{r}
summary(Leaf_Moist_Day1_Model)
summary(Leaf_Moist_Day2_Model)
```

p = 0.622, p - 0.0507

## 2.4. Evaluating SPAD Value by Treatment

#### Initial Visualization of SPAD Value by Treatment

```{r}
# Creating visualization of mean SPAD value for each treatment
SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  
  # Removing NA values with filter()
  filter(is.na(SPAD_Value) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Removing the plants with SPAD data but no leaves with filter()
  filter(Num_leaves > 0) |>
  
  # Generating summary statistics with summarise()
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(
    mean_SPAD = mean(SPAD_Value),
    sd_SPAD = sd(SPAD_Value),
    n = n(),
    se_SPAD = sd_SPAD/sqrt(n)
  ) |>
  
  # Creating column plot with error bars using ggplot() + geom_bar() +
  # geom_errorbar()
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = Treatment, y = mean_SPAD, fill = Treatment) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(
    ymin = mean_SPAD - se_SPAD,
    ymax = mean_SPAD + se_SPAD
    ),
    position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.2
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "SPAD Value"
  )
```

Column plot of mean SPAD value at each treatment, with standard error bars visualized at the top of each column. There appears to be some differences in SPAD value at each treatment, with NR and OS appearing lower on average than AC and DT.

#### Checking Prerequisites for ANOVA Testing

```{r}
# Creating backup SPAD data set with no NAs for testing using filter()
SPAD_Data_no_NA = SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  filter(is.na(SPAD_Value) == FALSE) |>
  filter(Num_leaves != 0)

# Visual verification
SPAD_Data_no_NA

# Generating mixed effects model for SPAD value data with lmer(), using Block, Date, and Multiple_Seedling as random effects
SPAD_Model = lmer(
  SPAD_Value ~ Treatment + (1|Block) + (1|Date) + (1|Multiple_Seedling),
  data = SPAD_Data_no_NA)

# Checking plot of residuals vs. fitted for our model with plot()
plot(SPAD_Model)

# Checking normality in SPAD_Value using hist()
hist(SPAD_Data_no_NA$SPAD_Value)
```

Our data appears to have homogeneity of variance and normality, so we can continue with a one-way ANOVA.

#### Conducting ANOVA Test

```{r}
# Displaying ANOVA table with anova()
anova(SPAD_Model)

# Conducting post-hoc test with emmeans() to fit the lmer() model, using Tukey adjustment
emmeans(SPAD_Model, pairwise ~ Treatment, adjust = "Tukey")
```

Our ANOVA table shows significant differences found amongst treatments (p = 2.299e-05), identified as AC - NR (p = 0.0010) and AC - OS (0.0019) after a Tukey post-hoc test.

#### Visualizing ANOVA Results

```{r}
# Creating visualization of mean SPAD value for each treatment
SPAD_Data_no_NA |>
  
  # Generating summary statistics with summarise()
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(
    mean_SPAD = mean(SPAD_Value),
    sd_SPAD = sd(SPAD_Value),
    n = n(),
    se_SPAD = sd_SPAD/sqrt(n)
  ) |>
  
  # Creating column plot with error bars using ggplot() + geom_bar() +
  # geom_errorbar()
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = Treatment, y = mean_SPAD, fill = Treatment) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(
    ymin = mean_SPAD - se_SPAD,
    ymax = mean_SPAD + se_SPAD
    ),
    position = position_dodge(0.9), width = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_text(
    label = c("AB", "[A]BCD", "BCD", "BCD"),
    vjust = -1.25, size = 3
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Mean SPAD Value"
  )
```

Column plot of average SPAD values between treatments, with standard error bars depicted at the top of each column. Results from a one-way ANOVA are denoted at the top of each column as well. The adult canopy treatment was found to differ from natural recruits and open sky treatments, specifically, while no differences were found between any of the other three treatments. Notably, the adult canopy and dead tree treatments were found to have a p-value of \~0.06 in their comparison, which is above the 0.05 threshold but close enough to still be noteworthy. It is possible that the adult canopy treatment has greener leaves due to the canopy overhead limiting the amount of light reaching the seedling, demanding a darker coloration to absorb more of the limited light reaching its leaves.

#### Checking Prerequisites for ANOVA Testing

```{r}
# Creating backup tibble with dead seedlings removed, using filter()
Height_Data_Alive = Height_Data_Clean |>
  filter(Seedling_Ht_cm > 0)

# Visual verification
Height_Data_Alive

# Generating mixed effects model for seedling height data with lmer(), using Block, Date, and Multiple_Seedling as random effects
Height_Model = lmer(
  Seedling_Ht_cm ~ Treatment + (1|Block) + (1|Date) + (1|Multiple_Seedling),
  data = Height_Data_Alive)

# Checking plot of residuals vs. fitted for our model with plot()
plot(Height_Model)
```

We can immediately see that there is not homogeneity of variance for our data. We will investigate visually.

```{r}
# Visually searching for outliers
Height_Data_Alive
```

There is no reason to remove outliers, so we will have to weight our lmer model to account for unequal variance.

# ASK ABOUT THIS DURING OFFICE HOURS

I need to weight this model for variance. It has a *weights* argument that needs a vector of values and I know the formula for weighting by variance is 1/Variance. I'm using varWeights with a varClasses function as an argument, selecting the specific function to fit the shape of the residuals, but want to know if I'm approaching this correctly.

```{r}
# Creating varClasses function fit to the shape of the Residuals plot, in this case varExp
Height_variance = varExp(Height_Data_Alive$Seedling_Ht_cm,
  ~Height_Data_Alive$Treatment)

# Generating mixed effects model for seedling height data with lmer(), using Block, Date, and Multiple_Seedling as random effects. Weights set using varWeights() on our varClasses model
Height_Model = lmer(
  Seedling_Ht_cm ~ Treatment + (1|Block) + (1|Date) + (1|Multiple_Seedling),
  data = Height_Data_Alive, weights = varWeights(Height_variance))

# Checking histogram of Seedling_Ht_cm with hist() to check for normality
hist(Height_Data_Alive$Seedling_Ht_cm)
```

Our data has a tail but appears mostly normal. We will proceed with a multiple-effects ANOVA.

#### Conducting ANOVA Test

```{r}
# Displaying ANOVA table with anova()
anova(Height_Model)

# Conducting post-hoc test with emmeans() to fit the lmer() model, using Tukey adjustment
emmeans(Height_Model, pairwise ~ Treatment, adjust = "Tukey")
```

Our ANOVA table shows significant differences found amongst treatments (p = 1.329e-07), identified as AC - NR (p = 0.0016), AC - OS (p = 0.0229), DT - NR (p = 0.0044), and DT-OS (p = 0.0246) after a Tukey post-hoc test.

#### Visualizing ANOVA Results

```{r}
Height_Data_Alive |>

  # Calculating summary statistics with summarise()
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(

    sd_Height = sd(Seedling_Ht_cm),
    n = n(),
    se_Height = sd_Height/sqrt(n)
  ) |>
  
  # Generating column plot with error bars using ggplot() + geom_col() +

  ggplot() +

  ),
```

Column plot of average seedling height between treatments, with standard error bars depicted at the top of each column. Results from a one-way multiple-effects ANOVA are denoted at the top of each column as well. The Adult Canopy/Dead Tree treatments were found to be significantly different from the Natural Recruit/Open Sky treatments, with the two pairs each being statistically indistinct from one another. It is possible that the Natural Recruit and Open Sky treatments had more space to grow by virtue of the former representing seedlings naturally selected for ideal conditions for growth and the latter being planted in open terrain.

## 2.6. Evaluating Leaf Count by Treatment

#### Initial Visualization of Leaf Count by Treatment

```{r}
# Creating visualization of mean leaf count value for each treatment
SPAD_Data_Clean |>
  
  # Removing plants without leaves and NA SPAD values using filter() to remain
  # consistent with our previous ANOVA testing on SPAD data 
  filter(Num_leaves > 0) |>
  filter(is.na(SPAD_Value) == FALSE) |>
  
  # Generating summary statistics with summarise()
  group_by(Treatment) |>
  summarise(
    mean_Leaf = mean(Num_leaves),
    sd_Leaf = sd(Num_leaves),
    n = n(),
    se_Leaf = sd_Leaf/sqrt(n)
  ) |>
  
  # Creating column plot with error bars using ggplot() + geom_bar() +
  # geom_errorbar()
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = Treatment, y = mean_Leaf, fill = Treatment) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(
    ymin = mean_Leaf - se_Leaf,

  ),
```

Column plot of mean leaf count at each treatment, with standard error bars visualized at the top of each column. The Natural Recruit treatment has a noticeably higher mean than all other treatments, with Open Sky lagging behind. Notably, the Adult Canopy treatment and Dead Tree treatment are equivalent here as observed in previous ANOVA tests on SPAD value and seedling height, with standard error for the other two treatments not being quite as high as it was for mean seedling heights.

#### Checking Prerequisites for ANOVA testing

Conveniently, we can reuse our SPAD data set copy from the SPAD ANOVA tests since it still retains data on leaf count. We will need to thin our leaf counts as done in our regression testing on leaf count, however.

```{r}
# Removing duplicated leaf count values with distinct()
Leaf_Model_Data = SPAD_Data_no_NA |>
  group_by(ID_num, Sapling_Num) |>
  distinct(Num_leaves, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Generating mixed effects model for leaf count data with lmer(), using Block, Date, and Multiple_Seedling as random effects

  Num_leaves ~ Treatment + (1|Block) + (1|Date) + (1|Multiple_Seedling),
  data = Leaf_Model_Data)

# Checking residuals vs. fitted plot with plot()
plot(Leaf_Model)
```

While this has reduced noise in our data, this still has unequal variance. We will need to weight our lmer model to account for this.

# Same issue as previous ANOVA

```{r}
Leaf_ANOVA_variance = varExp(Leaf_Model_Data$Num_leaves, ~Leaf_Model_Data$Treatment)

# Generating mixed effects model for leaf count data with lmer(), using Block, Date, and Multiple_Seedling as random effects. Weighted for variance with varWeights()
Leaf_Model = lmer(
  Num_leaves ~ Treatment + (1|Block) + (1|Date) + (1|Multiple_Seedling),
  data = Leaf_Model_Data, weights = varWeights(Leaf_ANOVA_variance))
```

results
